headline: Every Team Still 0-0, Still 0.0 Points, and Four Franchises Just Burned Waiver Priority on the Same Undrafted Running Back
meme_brief: The whole league is stuck in a scoreless purgatory where nobody has played a game yet, but that didn't stop four separate teams from racing to grab the exact same anonymous waiver-wire running back like it was a Black Friday doorbuster.
recap: Week 1 is, once again, a dead heat everywhere — every one of the six matchups finished 0.0 to 0.0, the second consecutive week the entire league has failed to score a single point. Chuba Bucky Doo's supposed dominance continues in the standings only, sitting at the top of nothing in particular, while the commissioner's own team joins the other eleven at a flat zero. There is no closest game because there is no game with any points in it. There is no blowout, because a blowout requires one side to have more than zero. The top scorer across the league is, mathematically, everyone and no one, tied at 0.0. As for worst bench decision — hard to bench-manage your way into a loss when the entire league's slate refuses to generate a single stat. This remains the fantasy equivalent of a rain delay that just keeps not ending.
transaction_desk:
The headline move of the week wasn't really a move — it was four of them, all the same. Joe Mama Angie Daddy, Meredith's Fan Club, mikelanta, and Pukachu Chews You all burned real waiver priority on the same depth-chart running back, Mike Washington, in what amounts to a four-way tie for a lottery ticket. Three of those four gave up nothing to get him; mikelanta had to drop the receiver it had just added days earlier to make room, which is either efficient roster churn or an admission the original pickup was a mistake before it ever played a snap. Joe Mama Angie Daddy also used priority on Malik Davis, spending real draft-order currency on a depth back with no guarantee of playing time — a real bet by rolling-waiver standards, not a free look.

Elsewhere the moves were lower-stakes. Chuba Bucky Doo cycled through the defense and tight end slots on the wire (added, then dropped, Hunter Henry within the same week window as picking up Chig Okonkwo) without spending priority — free, uncontested, low risk. Broke Dak Mountain added Najee Harris and Xavier Hutchinson off the wire at zero cost, which given that team's now-established habit of stockpiling names that immediately go dormant, continues to track. Silverbacks grabbed Hunter Henry for free the moment Chuba Bucky Doo cut him loose, which at minimum wins the week's most efficient recycling operation, if not yet any actual points.

standings_narrative: With every team sitting at 0-0 and every scoreboard reading zero, there is technically no playoff picture yet — six of these twelve teams will make it, and right now that is as true for Screaming Eagles as it is for anyone posting real numbers eventually will. The only separation in the league so far is behavioral: who is spending waiver priority (Joe Mama Angie Daddy, Meredith's Fan Club, mikelanta, Pukachu Chews You) and who is sitting on their hands (Waffle House, Geoff Collins Suvivor, demon44, Dak's Stack, Screaming Eagles). None of it means anything until points actually get recorded, but the early bubble, if you want to call it that, is going to be about who wasted their draft-order leverage on a running back four other teams also wanted.
look_ahead: Next week's matchups are the same six pairings, and the obvious hope around the league is that somebody, anybody, finally gets a stat line that isn't a zero. The four-team scramble for the same waiver running back will start to sort itself out by usage, and it will be worth tracking whether that spent priority produces anything or just moves those four rosters toward the back of the line for nothing. Chuba Bucky Doo will again enter as the only unbeaten team in football scoring no points, which is either a bit or a genuine season-long identity at this point.
